deep.reconstruction:
Setting: a category A with set of arrows Fl(A). For a class Φ ⊂ Fl(A), Grothendieck defines Φ* as the arrows having the left lifting property (LLP) with respect to Φ, and Φ_* as the arrows having the right lifting property (RLP) with respect to Φ. This is the Galois connection given by the orthogonality relation u ⧄ v. A class is left saturated if Φ = Ψ* for some Ψ, equivalently Φ = (Φ_*)*. It is right saturated if Ψ = Φ_*, equivalently Ψ = (Ψ*)_*. As for any Galois connection, Φ ⊂ (Φ_*)* and Ψ ⊂ (Ψ*)_*, and Φ ↦ Φ_* and Ψ ↦ Ψ* are inverse order-reversing bijections between left-saturated and right-saturated classes. The margin notes that saturated classes are closed under direct factors (retracts).

Factorisation property: for a mutually orthogonal pair (Φ, Ψ), meaning Φ ⊂ Ψ* or equivalently Ψ ⊂ Φ_*, every f factors as f = p∘i with i ∈ Φ and p ∈ Ψ.

Proposition (the retract argument): if the factorisation property holds, then Φ = Ψ* iff Φ is closed under retracts, and dually Ψ = Φ_* iff Ψ is closed under retracts. Proof sketch: given u ∈ Ψ*, factor u = p∘i. Lifting u against p exhibits u as a retract of i.

Grothendieck calls (Φ, Ψ) a 'dual pair (localizers)' when Φ = Ψ* and Ψ = Φ_*. A 'Quillen pair' is a dual pair with factorisation, equivalently an orthogonal pair with factorisation and both classes retract-closed. In modern language this is exactly a weak factorization system.

'Quillen triple' (C, F, W): (a) W satisfies 2-out-of-3 (Quillen's M5) and is closed under direct factors; (b) (C, TF := F∩W) and (TC := C∩W, F) are Quillen pairs, encoding M1 and M2 together with retract-closure. Retract-closure need only be checked for C and F, given it for W. A middle note says the retract condition on W should be unnecessary once (b) is assumed. This is the modern definition of a (closed) model category via two weak factorization systems plus 2-out-of-3.

Consequences:
- f ∈ W iff f = p∘i with i ∈ TC and p ∈ TF.
- W is 'strongly saturated': f ∈ W iff γ_W(f) is an isomorphism in W⁻¹A.

The margin adds that this holds at any rate if finite sums and fibered sums (and products) exist, i.e. Quillen's M0. The page serves as a recollection of Quillen's homotopical algebra in Grothendieck's own axiomatics, written on the back of a June 1982 Cray printout. That places it in the run-up to Pursuing Stacks, where model categories and 'localizers' play a central role.
errors: No substantive errors. The equivalence 'Quillen pair = orthogonal pair + factorisation + retract-closure of both classes' is correct (standard retract argument).

The strong-saturation claim is correct for closed model categories with M0 (Quillen 1967). Grothendieck himself flags that he is relying on existence of finite (co)limits; without M0 the standard proof via cylinders/path objects is not available as stated.
The middle remark that retract-closure of W is redundant given (b) and 2-out-of-3 is correct but only asserted, not proved on the page.

missed.claim: Grothendieck observes, c. 1982, that the retract-closure condition on W in a model category should be superfluous once both factorization pairs are assumed. This anticipates the Joyal–Tierney remark (2007) that the retract axiom for weak equivalences is redundant. It is only stated, not proved, so it is a minor priority note rather than a new result.
missed.quote: it should not be necessary here to put the condition direct factors on W, if we assume b)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it shows Grothendieck independently recasting model categories as a pair of weak factorization systems plus 2-out-of-3, and spotting the redundancy of an axiom, well before this became the textbook formulation.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a clean, standard recollection of Quillen's model-category axiomatics in the language of lifting-property Galois connections and weak factorization systems. That formulation is now textbook, though slightly ahead of its time for 1982. The only mildly notable point is the unproved remark that retract-closure of W is redundant, later published by Joyal–Tierney.
transcription_corrections: The class written as \mathcal{F} is most likely a script Φ (Phi), paired with Ψ; the line 'Ψ = Φ_* for some Φ' confirms the Φ/Ψ notation.
The left-margin note reads approximately: 'Right saturation Ψ ⇒ stability by direct factors (i.e. retractions); dually for left'.
In 'W saturated (M5) (two in W, and the third ...)' the parenthetical is the 2-out-of-3 property; the insertion 'and stable by direct factors' is written above.
The bottom-left margin reads approximately: 'true at any rate if in A finite direct and fibered sums exist (M0)'.
The 'TC, TF' in item b) is written under the struck text and refers to C∩W and F∩W.
